coracias-chauvireae:study:1.title: A New Fossil Species of Roller (Aves: Coraciidae) from the Lower Pleistocene of Crimea (Doklady Biological Sciences, 2026)

facts.statement: The species was described in 2026 by N. Zelenkov using a tarsometatarsus fossil from the Early Pleistocene Taurida Cave in central Crimea.
facts.quote: It was described in 2026 by N. Zelenkov based on a tarsometatarsus found from the Early Pleistocene deposits of the Taurida Cave in the central Crimean Peninsula.

facts.statement: Coracias chauvireae is an extinct bird belonging to the family Coraciidae, commonly known as rollers.
facts.quote: Coracias chauvireae is an extinct species of bird in the family Coraciidae (rollers).

facts.statement: This species represents the oldest known fossil evidence of the genus Coracias found in Eurasia.
facts.quote: It is currently the oldest evidence of the genus Coracias from Eurasia.

facts.statement: The fossil record for this species dates to the Pleistocene epoch.
Fossils of this species have been found in Crimea.
The species was designated as a new species (Sp. nov) upon its description.
The taxonomic status of the species is currently considered valid.

rejected.statement: The species is closely related to the clade containing the modern lilac-breasted roller and European roller, a lineage that originated in Africa.
rejected.quote: It is closely related to the clade containing the modern lilac-breasted roller (C. caudatus) and European roller (C. garrulus), which originated in Africa.
